review: reciprocal-conversation@1 (handler long.reciprocal-conversation, scope long-ex26, learning 1 with no study energy, prerequisite and dependency tell, references {} since no parameter names a target, execution duration 1, visualComponents [] with view metadata on every event, no satisfaction rule) is a two-person conversation session built on tell: every spoken step (propose, join, resume, contribute) calls tell's own handler (expression.tell of foundation-expression@1, taken from expressionFoundation for the installed scope), so its told event is delivered by tell's own after-round delivery to exactly tell's hearers (every other living person within config.vision = 5 at the end of the round, seen or not) with tell's heard events and bounded heard lists (tested against a plain tell at 4.99 and 5.01); a contribution is exactly the person's words (at most 240 characters), while propose, join and resume say a short line naming the session id and topic plus optional words, within 240. Each spoken mode costs what tell costs (1 round, 0 energy, 0 material, tested against the same tells by hand); pause, leave and cancel say nothing and cost no energy, but like every action they occupy the person's action for that round, because the kernel runs exactly one action per person per round. Range: propose needs the invited person alive, seen now (v7Observe) and within 5, and join, resume, contribute and pause need the other participant alive and within 5 at the start of the round, checked before anything about the session is revealed; a person out of range gets the same answer as for an unknown id or person. The session record is hidden world state (reciprocal-conversation:sessions) written only after the round's actions, so simultaneous steps of both people never conflict; each person's own record (reciprocal-conversation:work:open, shown with active work, and reciprocal-conversation:last) holds only their own acts, the other's acceptances and words they actually heard and changes that happened within 5 of them: an invited person learns of a session only by hearing its invitation or the proposer's join; a leave, cancel or death of the other person more than 5 away is disclosed only when they are within 5 again or at the expiry round, and until then the record stays as it would have been (an active one pauses for range); the other person's pause reasons show only within 5; every notice is a positionless event seen only by its own person. Lifecycle: proposing is not consent; the session becomes active at the end of a round in which both have joined with the exact topic, each heard the other's join, both are alive within 5 and neither is at an urgent risk; while active, a round that is not a step of that session, wait (silence) or a refused step of this interface pauses it, as do being more than 5 apart and an urgent risk (the kernel's lines also used by bounded-resource-search@1: health <= 60, satiety <= 8, body temperature 10 or more from 22, or an injury in the last round); resume needs both people again, each heard by the other; leave or cancel by either participant, death (onDeath) or the expiry round (proposal round plus rounds, 1 to 20, not extended by pausing) ends it, and words already said stay heard. A contribution is committed only when the other participant actually heard it (their heard event is the delivery evidence); otherwise it is reported as interrupted and does not count. A reciprocal exchange is recorded once per utterance pair, with both event ids, speakers, listeners, topic, rounds and heard evidence, when a committed contribution names in respondsTo an earlier committed utterance of the other person (which the responder heard) and uses new words, so acceptances, proposals, identical retries and simultaneous unrelated utterances never form one, and each first utterance completes at most one exchange. Modeling assumptions: the topic is fixed per session and must be named exactly in join, so a new topic needs a new session that both join independently; resume is spoken (a short tell) so that reaffirmation is audible like join; the session id is assigned as session-<round>-<proposer>; a person may have one open session they proposed and any number they were invited to; wait is the silent turn and any other action counts as another action; invite is not called (people may still use it themselves) and message delivery is not used as evidence; there are no group sessions or new media; the hidden record of a closed session is kept 40 rounds after its end once nobody's own record of it is open, while its events stay in the event journal. No reward: no satisfaction rule, no event carries a qualified flag or numeric progress, practiceEvidence is the exchange notice without a qualified flag, and vitals, wellbeing, mood, pleasure, routine and progress accounting equal those of the same words by tell (tested); nothing is created, moved, granted or charged beyond tell. The ability serializes to 2235 code units (limit 3500), every earlier package is byte-identical by its id@version digest, and the bounded-resource-search test now asserts that it is the first long-ex26 package rather than the last package overall.
